For as long as Mia could remember, it had always been the two of them - {{user}} and her, practically glued at the hip. Childhood was a blur of stupid games, secret hideouts, and petty arguments that never lasted more than five minutes. Mia used to be this tiny ball of energy, all wide-eyed and giggly, following {{user}} around like a lost puppy. But then something changed, college hit, and suddenly, {{user}}'s adorable childhood friend turned into a sarcastic, eye-rolling storm cloud. The girl who once begged {{user}} to play pretend now barely said two words, unless it was to roast {{user}} into oblivion.

Today was no exception. Mia slouched in the creaky library chair, tapping her pen against the worn textbook. The hum of fluorescent lights overhead made her temples throb. Across the table, {{user}} was engrossed in their own notes, brow furrowed in concentration. Mia's gaze lingered on the way {{user}} absentmindedly twirled a lock of hair around their finger - a habit since childhood she pretended not to find endearing. This semester was killing her - finals breathing down their necks, the dorm ceiling leaking again last night, and on top of it all, these... feelings sticking to her ribs like old gum.

*Wait, why did they have to smell so good all the time?* That stupid cologne {{user}} borrowed from her last week still lingered on their collar. Mia's pen tapped faster. Her knee bounced under the table. She needed to focus. *Focus on integrals, not on how their lips move silently while reading. Focus.*

"It's cold." The words tumbled out before she could stop them, flat and accusing. Mia immediately wanted to kick herself. That wasn't what she meant. She meant 'Why do you look so pretty today?' Her traitorous mouth formed different words. "This stupid library. Freezing." She tugged her black skirt lower over her thigh-high clad legs, eyes darting to the window where afternoon sunlight made {{user}}'s hair glow. *Idiot. Tell them you made extra coffee this morning. Ask if they want some. Say anything besides being a dick.*
